dialogues.text: The lord himself has heard your name spoken well.
You keep the manor in good order. I notice.
Work hard and you may eat.
Keep your head down and pay what's owed.
You're a stain on this manor. Watch yourself.
The steward looks you over without comment.
The church lights a candle for you, friend.
Your generosity is remembered in our prayers.
A donation to the church is never forgotten.
You have turned your back on the church's call.
The bishop will hear of this.
Father Tomas regards you calmly.
Hilda claps your shoulder - you're one of us now.
Folks speak well of you at the well.
Cold spring, but the turnips will hold.
You've been keeping strange company, I hear.
Keep away from my door.
Hilda nods as you pass.
Cedric shares his bread - you've earned it.
The village sings your praise at the inn.
Keep an eye on your coin pouch.
We all saw what you did. We don't forget.
Don't come any closer.
Cedric watches you warily.
Marta laughs and waves you over.
You've a good name in the village, friend.
I'm just a simple farmer.
Best you keep your distance from me.
The village is tired of your kind.
Marta gives a thin smile.
Bram insists you share his fire tonight.
The village owes you thanks, and says so.
Heard there's trouble on the roads.
I'd think twice before walking through the village.
You're not welcome at the crossroads.
Bram looks through you.
Three years running, now - you've kept pace with me the whole way. That's more than most manage.
Your rows are straighter this month. I counted.
Six furlongs sown between us, near enough. Fair spring for it.
You're behind. I'm not saying by how much.
There's no plot there. I don't see one.
Edith counts something under her breath and doesn't look up.
A sack in, four stone back this time - don't tell the steward I said so.
Bring it early next time. I'll grind it first, not last.
A sack in, three stone back. Same as always.
You'll wait your turn like everyone else.
Full multure, no exceptions. Not for you.
Osric weighs your sack without a word.
A rare find, they tell me - blessed be a lucky forager.
Steward Aldric speaks well of you. I mind him closely on that.
Aldric doesn't complain about you. That's something, from him.
I couldn't say. Aldric hasn't said much either way.
Aldric's had words about you. I just weigh what's put on the scale.
Aldric's warned me about you. I'd rather not linger over the count.
The young clerk keeps his eyes on the scale, careful not to make an error.
